evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a date with no time; a datetime string was rejected with 400.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 {"dueDate":"2026-01-01"} returned 200 with dueDate 2026-01-01. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null.
evidence.AC3: POST and PATCH with dueDate "2026-02-30", "01.02.2026", "foo" and "2026-10-14T10:00:00" all returned 400 with the error 'dueDate must be a valid date (yyyy-MM-dd)'. dueDate 5 (a number) also returned 400, with a JSON read error.
evidence.AC4: Today in UTC is 2026-10-14. I created todos with due dates 2026-10-01 (not done), 2026-12-01, 2026-10-14 (today), none, and 2026-09-01 (marked done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the 2026-10-01 todo. The future, today, no-date and done-past todos were excluded.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed 'fällig 01.10.2026', 'fällig 01.12.2026', 'fällig 14.10.2026' and 'fällig 01.09.2026' next to the matching todos. The todo without a due date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the page only the 'past' todo (due 01.10.2026, not done) carried the text 'überfällig'. The future, today, no-date and done-past todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Clicking it reduced the list to only the 'past' todo.
